title: Crash density: painted vs. protected lanes
description: Painted-only bike lanes see 5.1 cyclist crashes per km vs 10.2 on protected lanes — 0.5x the density, raw counts not normalized by ridership.
caveat: Raw counts overrepresent high-traffic corridors; no volume normalization. Dooring crashes are undercounted citywide.

title: Highest crash-density corridors
description: Top corridors by cyclist crashes per km of bikeway: Dearborn St (17.41/km); Kinzie St (11.75/km); Wood St (9.83/km); Stony Island Ave (8.65/km); Vincennes Ave (8.12/km).
caveat: Raw counts, not normalized by bike volume. Dooring is undercounted.

title: Ward concentration
description: 5 of 50 wards account for 45% of located cyclist crashes: Ward 34 (132), Ward 33 (131), Ward 38 (129), Ward 39 (83), Ward 23 (62).
caveat: Ward totals reflect where people ride most, not only where streets are worst.

title: Dooring: the number that is too low
description: Only 73 crashes carry a dooring flag. Dooring is structurally excluded from 'reportable' crash records unless damage/injury thresholds are met, so true dooring risk — especially on painted-lane corridors — is higher than any number on this site.
caveat: Structural undercount; treat as a floor, never a rate.

title: What cyclists collide with
description: Most common motor-vehicle unit types in cyclist crashes: Passenger (493), Truck - Single Unit (243), Van/Mini-Van (236).
caveat: Unit types as recorded by responding officers; fleet mix not normalized.
